label: Consolidated Edition

summary: MEPC has progressively tightened Annex VI through EEXI, CII rating and the 2023 GHG Strategy's push toward net-zero around 2050; ECA sulphur/NOx Tier III boundaries continue to expand — MEPC 84 (27 April-1 May 2026) designated a further NOx/SOx Emission Control Area covering the Norwegian Sea and Canadian Arctic (NOx Tier III from 1 March 2026 for qualifying new ships, 0.10% sulphur fuel from 1 March 2027) and a new North-East Atlantic ECA due to enter into force 1 September 2027. The biggest pending change remains the IMO Net-Zero Framework — a global fuel standard (well-to-wake greenhouse-gas fuel intensity limits) plus a GHG pricing/remedial-unit mechanism for large ships (5,000 GT+), to be inserted as a new Annex VI Chapter 5. MEPC 83 (April 2025) approved it for large oceangoing ships, but the extraordinary session called to formally adopt it in October 2025 adjourned without agreement, and MEPC 84 (April-May 2026) also closed without an adoption vote; the Committee instead set up an intersessional working group meeting in September and November 2026 to narrow differences ahead of a possible vote at MEPC 85 (late November/early December 2026) — as of mid-2026 the Framework remains approved-but-not-yet-adopted — confirm the live status before the exam.

summary: Parliament passed the Merchant Shipping Bill, 2024 on 11 August 2025 and it received Presidential assent on 18 August 2025 as the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 (Act No. 24 of 2025), restructuring and replacing the 1958 Act — compressing roughly 561 sections into about 325 sections across 16 parts. It formally renames India's maritime regulator from Director General of Shipping to Director General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), and is intended to harmonise domestic law more closely with current SOLAS, MARPOL, STCW and BWM Convention obligations while modernising seafarer-welfare and casualty-investigation provisions. The Central Government has since brought the Act into force with effect from 15 March 2026 (notification S.O. 1244(E) dated 10 March 2026), so it now supersedes the 1958 Act as the operative statute, with subordinate rules under the new Act being notified progressively through 2026. Part-by-part decomposition (the Act runs to 16 Parts) is deliberately not attempted in this repository yet - no official gazette text of the Act is held locally, and inventing Part titles/numbers without a primary source would risk exactly the kind of fabrication this repository is built to avoid. This entry stays at document level until that text is available.

summary: Explains the new SOLAS regulation II-1/3-13 on lifting appliances, anchor handling winches and associated loose gear, adopted together with IMO guidelines for lifting appliances (MSC.1/Circ.1663) and for anchor handling winches (MSC.1/Circ.1662), all in force from 1 January 2026. Lifting appliances and winches installed on or after that date must be designed, installed and load-tested to Recognized Organization requirements and permanently marked with their safe working load; equipment already installed must be tested, thoroughly examined and SWL-documented by the first SAFCON renewal survey on or after 1 January 2026, unless already covered by a valid test certificate under another recognized instrument such as ILO Convention No. 152. Five-yearly load retesting and annual thorough examination apply to all such equipment regardless of installation date.

summary: Clarifies, under STCW Regulation III/7 and Code Section A-III/7, how a General Purpose rating who has obtained an Electro-Technical Rating (ETR) Certificate of Proficiency and the required sea service may progress to the Electro-Technical Officer (ETO) course and CoC examination, updating the eligibility criteria first set out in DGS Training Circular No. 12 of 2020. It removes the earlier age restriction on ETR CoP holders enrolling in the ETO course once they have the necessary sea service, and confirms that an approved ETR Training and Assessment Record (TAR) Book must be verified by an MMD assessing officer before the ETR CoP itself is issued.

New regulation II-1/3-13 (lifting appliances and anchor handling winches) enters into force, requiring design/construction to classification-society or equivalent standards, load testing, and periodic thorough examination of ship's cranes, stores cranes and similar lifting gear.
